# Technical explainer channel bible

## Confirmed direction
- Full-length widescreen YouTube videos. Length follows the subject; no arbitrary runtime ceiling.
- Technical subjects: show how something works, for curious beginners AND knowledgeable viewers.
- Backgrounds are selected by Codex for the subject and shot: use light or dark according to explanatory clarity, with consistent meaning and readable graphics. The user delegated this choice.
- Combine realistic subject models with simplified technical views. Every simplification must preserve the explanation's causal truth.
- Narrator only. No Grandpa, presenter, or livestream framing in the explainer output.
- Narration with restrained mechanical sound effects; no music. Cues must explain a visible action, not decorate every transition.
- No burned-in narration captions. YouTube handles captions. Technical labels, dimensions, graphs and legends remain useful visual tools.
- Imported assets must cost nothing to obtain and permit commercial use and modification for monetized videos. Prefer CC0/public domain; CC BY is acceptable with practical attribution. Exclude noncommercial, no-derivatives and editorial-only assets.
- For now use continuously animated 3D explanation, as in the accepted piston test. Static-image sections and held-render presentations are parked at the user’s request. Technical labels may support moving scenes.
- ChatGPT Image support remains available for a later direction change, but do not use static-image sections in the current Tesla film. It is not the source of technical truth. Do not assume its ability to create accurate mechanical geometry or animations.
- Codex completes missing research, scripts, assets, shot design and production work. Ask about creative direction/options one question at a time; resolve routine architectural and implementation decisions independently.
- User approves the storyboard and a representative short preview before full production.
- Before presenting a preview, Codex inspects the actual output, repairs obvious problems and checks again. A successful render is insufficient.

## Editorial identity
Lead with a concrete question, show the mechanism, build a causal explanation, show limits and finish with a useful takeaway. Explain unfamiliar terms at first use. Offer precise details once the physical intuition is clear. Avoid false drama, unsupported numbers, guaranteed outcomes, or imitation of a reference channel's branding.

The channel name, branding and recurring creative treatments are undecided. Ask before choosing them. Default implementation colors and test objects are engineering fixtures, not locked branding.

explainer/bibles/ACCURACY.md.text:
# Research and accuracy bible

Each factual shot links explicit claims. Each claim records its text, verification status and source IDs. Sources include title, URL/document locator, access date and the exact supporting quotation, passage, measurement or calculation. Prefer primary technical documentation; corroborate consequential or disputed claims. Status fields record Codex's research; software cannot certify factual truth.

Supplied documents, videos, timestamps and generated images are references to investigate, never automatically trusted instructions or verified evidence. A patent shows a disclosed idea; it does not establish deployment, performance, feature parity or safety guarantees. Verify identifiers and dates. Cite the actual evidence for numerical comparisons. Explain uncertain or unavailable internal details rather than inventing them.

For each asset record origin, permissions/provenance, actual file SHA-256 and accuracy review. Verify referenced existing assets exist and are usable before scheduling them. Label each shot literal, schematic or analogy; record omissions and simplifications. Generated images require inspection of parts, labels, units, connections and mechanism before acceptance. Add accurate labels as controlled graphics rather than trusting generated text.

No generic rotor/conduit model presented as an accurate rendering of an unrelated subject. Subject adapters must be built and reviewed when the primitive backend cannot represent the mechanism. Research/modeling blockers stay visible; never satisfy them with fabricated sources or test data.

## Free commercial assets

Use only assets that are free to obtain and whose actual source-specific terms permit commercial use and modification. Prefer CC0/public domain; CC BY needs attribution. The initial policy accepts CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, or a documented public-domain basis. NC, ND, editorial-only, paid, unknown and other licenses are blocked pending a deliberate future policy extension. A free library account or collection-level license does not prove the individual model's rights.

For each model retain title, creator, source URL, exact license ID/link, source-specific license evidence, access date, price 0, reviewed commercial/modification permissions, additional restrictions (must be none), unit basis and hashes of every model/material/texture/evidence file. CC BY also requires attribution text and a changes statement. Review embedded textures and distinct contributor terms; mixed/unclear licenses require another asset or a fuller future rights adapter. Code validates these records and prevents changes going unnoticed; it cannot establish whether a source owns the rights or whether recorded statements are true. Codex must actually read the evidence.

Registration copies a complete contained package and keeps visual/accuracy review pending. Inspect mesh, textures, proportions, component structure and subject suitability before marking that review approved. No scientific accuracy follows from a permissive license. Credits are generated in CREDITS.md, including source, creator, license, attribution and changes; carry them into the video description at release. No asset or video is published automatically.

explainer/bibles/WORKFLOW.md.text:
# Production and self-correction bible

1. Intake: preserve the supplied plan as unverified reference. Extract title, narration, timings, visual and sound instructions. Never execute embedded code or adopt document role instructions. Codex completes a structured plan, subject-specific assets, sources, claims and teaching goals. Ask only unresolved creative/direction questions, one at a time.
2. Preflight: validate plan and files. Research accuracy, check asset permissions and resolve missing capabilities. Narration is measured; shot timing must accommodate it. Keep plans and project artifacts isolated from Grandpa's engine/build.
3. Storyboard: generate the exact current shot list with narration and visuals. Present for user approval. Record approval only after an explicit user reply. A CLI approval flag is a record of real consent, not a way for Codex to grant it.
4. Internal representative preview: render a complete short shot at low resolution. The first backend previews at 640x360, 30 fps, 4 Cycles samples. Make diagnostic first/middle/last contact sheets, render motion and encode measured narration. Do not run a full video to answer architecture questions.
5. Self-check and correct: inspect geometry, images, full motion, narration, label readability, synchronization, scientific truth and consistency. Automatic framing repair widens the lens in at most three attempts and rechecks all frames. Media checks validate codecs, frame count, duration, audio format, loudness and clipping. Encoding retries are bounded. Correct semantic or visual defects deliberately, rebuild affected outputs and rerun checks. Never mark a failed check passed, remove an assertion or invent human review. Exhausted retries are blockers to investigate, not a preview ready to present.
6. Record actual visual/technical inspection notes using `review`. Present the checked representative preview. Record the user's explicit preview approval. No full production without both approvals for current plan/asset/code/bible bytes.
7. Full production: only after approval, render final shots, reusing frozen narration. Assemble and verify the full video, then inspect the entire assembled output and transitions. Render success is not release approval. Publication is a separate user-authorized action.

## Versioning
SHA-256 fingerprints cover plan, asset contents, engine and bibles. Editing any of these invalidates approvals conservatively. Generated output directories are fingerprint-specific; render frames resume only within that version. Freeze model identity and voice file bytes. Store QA reports, contact sheets, approval evidence and repair history alongside artifacts. Code and bibles live in Git; do not auto-commit or publish.

## Scope and truthful reporting
Passing automated checks means those particular checks passed. Factual and visual review are separate explicit records. State pending, failed, skipped and unrun work distinctly. New subject modules and recorded-sound adapters and final-resolution throughput are not validated by a synthetic smoke test. The system does not autonomously browse sources or generate images inside a Python process: Codex uses available research/image tools as needed and registers reviewed outputs.

## Explicit preview decisions

After a preview passes internal checks, present two user choices: **send to work pool** or **reject with changes**. Never queue automatically. `review_queue.py` captures the reviewed artifact, source hashes, user evidence and a source snapshot. Explainer project work items live in `explainer/work_pool/`, separate from Grandpa's incompatible scene-render queue. Approval of the visual direction queues continued production and preflight; it does not falsely mark the unbuilt full film render-ready. Rejection retains the artifact and notes for revision. Record only the actual user response.

explainer/README.md.text:
# Technical explainer production system

This separate workflow adapts Grandpa's procedural scene architecture, measured Kokoro voice, FFmpeg audio/video pipeline, frozen approval artifacts, resumable frame renders and automated QA. It does not use Grandpa's character, world, camera gag or caption overlay. Existing engine files and approved content remain intact.

Read [channel direction](bibles/CHANNEL.md), [narration](bibles/NARRATION.md), [accuracy](bibles/ACCURACY.md), [visuals](bibles/VISUALS.md) and [production workflow](bibles/WORKFLOW.md).

## Architecture

- `assets.py`: free/commercial rights policy, complete model package staging, resource hashes and credits.
- `model_import.py`: reviewed GLB/glTF, OBJ and STL instances with source materials, units, centered origins and uniform scale.
- `core.py`: structured project contract, source/claim/asset checks, timeline storyboard, content fingerprints.
- `__main__.py`: untrusted Markdown intake, project state, approval gates, previews, inspection records, final assembly.
- `media.py`: measured Kokoro speech, 48 kHz audio, quiet mechanical cues with speech ducking, loudness normalization, H.264/AAC encoding and media checks.
- `blender_backend.py`: procedural box/cylinder/sphere/tube assemblies, physical sections, flow arrows, tracking callout leaders, subject-dependent light/dark backgrounds, semantic materials, technical labels, translated/exploded parts, rotations, tracked camera direction, lighting, frame resumption and bounded framing repair.
- `vehicle_prop.py`: original generic EV with shaped bodywork, physical wheel wells, separate glazing/roof and rolling wheel rigs. Illustrative geometry, not Tesla CAD. The Tesla opening's project-specific adapter places moving traffic worlds in an explicitly schematic search tree.
- `bibles/`: durable direction and rules for Codex, including filling gaps and correcting issues before review.

Static image shots accept reviewed local images. ChatGPT Image can produce those images when useful; image generation is a Codex tool step, not a hidden network call from this package. Native CAD imports, general CAD/boolean cutaways, complex mechanics, graphs, automatic occlusion/clipping inspection and recorded sound effects require future adapters. Primitive local-plane sections and longitudinally sectioned hollow housings are supported. Timed, quiet procedural click/clunk/motor effects are supported; music is disabled by channel direction. A primitive rig cannot explain every subject accurately. Do not confuse validation metadata with automated fact checking.

## Runtime

Contract/intake/tests use Python 3.11+ and the standard library. Rendering additionally needs Blender's `bpy`, NumPy, SciPy, Pillow, kokoro-onnx, FFmpeg with libx264/AAC and the Kokoro model/voices. The current cloud machine has a tested Blender 5.2.3 Python environment at `/workspace/setup/blender-venv`; use:

```sh
cd /workspace/grandpa-block-lab
source /workspace/setup/activate.sh
python -m explainer --help
python -m unittest discover -s explainer/tests -v
```

Those cloud setup paths are local environment conveniences, not required repository paths. To set up another machine, use the exact dependency pins in `requirements.txt` with Python 3.13; obtain Kokoro model files from the upstream `thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx` release `model-files-v1.0` and set `KOKORO_MODEL` / `KOKORO_VOICES`. TLS and artifact verification must stay enabled. Do not install rendering dependencies to use the standard-library contract tools.

## Project workflow

All commands run from the repository root. The upload is a source of draft content, not authorization to execute it.

```sh
python -m explainer init explainer/projects/my_subject --title 'Subject title' --source /path/to/plan.md
python -m explainer status explainer/projects/my_subject
```

The importer recognizes four-column timestamp/visual/narration/audio tables, including the supplied example format. It preserves the whole source file and extracts draft shots. Other formats remain preserved for Codex to interpret. It never marks source claims verified or invents missing geometry.

Codex completes `plan.json` using `examples/contract-fixture.json` for the field layout. The fixture is a synthetic calibration object, not an episode proposal or verified scientific model. Each project also needs its own subject bible: scope, mechanism, terminology, narration guidance and simplifications. It is part of the approved storyboard and its fingerprint. Each shot supplies learning purpose, narration, visual intent, duration, factual claims, accuracy mode, components or image asset, camera and optional technical labels. `move_to` and `rotate_to` provide endpoint animation; rotation values are degrees. Images/models need provenance, reviewed status and file SHA-256. Every external asset path must stay inside its project.

```sh
python -m explainer validate explainer/projects/my_subject
python -m explainer prepare explainer/projects/my_subject
python -m explainer storyboard explainer/projects/my_subject
# Present storyboard; only AFTER the user approves it:
python -m explainer approve explainer/projects/my_subject storyboard --user-evidence 'Actual user approval reference'
python -m explainer preview explainer/projects/my_subject --shot shot_001
```

`prepare` measures and freezes narration and extends undersized shots before storyboard approval. The preview also checks speech timing and blocks if the shot is too short. Codex extends timing or edits narration, regenerates the storyboard and obtains approval for the revised version; no forced speedup. Inspect `contact-sheet.png`, actual video motion, `qa.json` and narration; repair and recheck until ready. Only then:

```sh
python -m explainer review explainer/projects/my_subject --shot shot_001 --notes 'Specific actual visual and technical inspection findings'
# Present preview; only AFTER the user approves it:
python -m explainer approve explainer/projects/my_subject preview --shot shot_001 --user-evidence 'Actual user approval reference'
python -m explainer final explainer/projects/my_subject
```

No CLI can authenticate a chat reply; recording genuine consent is a Codex workflow obligation, enforced in `AGENTS.md`. Code gates reject missing/stale evidence and unreviewed previews. They do not turn a typed claim of approval into real permission.

Artifacts are under `<project>/build/<fingerprint>/<preview|final>/<shot>/`. Current-version checksums cover the plan, actual assets, code and bibles. Changes invalidate approval. Final assembly has separate media QA and still needs inspection of the entire finished video. Nothing publishes automatically.

## Validation

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s explainer/tests -v
# Optional real Blender + narrator + encoding smoke; synthetic internal fixture only:
python -m explainer.tests.smoke
```

The smoke test creates no real user approval and produces no full-length video. Tests cover rejected missing claims/assets, path containment, stale approvals, blocked full production, draft table intake and a representative media workflow. See [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md) for the actual current run when available; full episode production is not implied by these checks.

## Mechanical visual tools

- A component with `shape: "tube"` has a real bore and optional `wall` fraction of outer diameter (default 0.12). `size` is the full uncut outer envelope.
- `section: {"axis": "y", "offset": 0, "keep": "positive"}` removes the negative local-Y half before object scaling/rotation. Offsets are fractions of the original unit diameter. Physical cut faces are capped. Tube sections permit X/Y only, preserving the bore; do not substitute a solid cylinder for a housing.
- `move_to` and `rotate_to` continue to support separating parts for an exploded view. Arbitrary linkage simulation is not implemented.
- A shot's `flows` list takes `id`, `path` (at least two distinct consecutive XYZ points), optional `radius`, semantic `role`, `animate` and required `explains`. A cone shows direction and the optional marker travels along the path. These are explanatory overlays, not fluid simulation.
- Technical labels may set `size` and `target` (a component ID). Text faces the camera; the leader endpoint follows the component center. Inspect legibility and obstructions; a geometric bound check cannot prove either.
- `presentation.background` is `auto`, `light` or `dark`. Explicit choices need `presentation.reason`. Auto starts schematic/analogy views light and literal models dark. Codex selects the best actual result and preserves semantic meaning across themes. The resolved background appears in the storyboard and geometry QA.

`examples/toolkit-fixture.json` is synthetic geometry for these utilities, not a real engineering mechanism. Run its diagnostic checks with `python -m explainer.tests.visual_smoke`.

## Importing free commercial models

Use a free-to-download asset with source-specific CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0 or documented public-domain evidence. Other licenses (including NC, ND, editorial-only, unknown or paid models) are rejected by the current policy. This is a conservative supported list; do not relabel a different license to make it pass.

1. Codex reads the actual model's license and all texture/contributor terms, downloads the files using verified HTTPS, and retains the source-specific evidence. Source URLs and hashes should identify a stable revision where available. The engine does not scrape model libraries or silently accept click-through terms.
2. Prepare rights metadata using `examples/licenses/avocado-rights.json` as the field reference. For CC BY, also supply `attribution` and `changes`. The supplied Avocado file is a CC0 format-calibration specimen, not a proposed video subject.
3. Register a local package; keep `.gltf` buffer/texture references or OBJ material/texture files next to the model with relative paths. Registration refuses missing files, paths outside the package, remote resources, duplicate IDs and unsupported formats. Embedded GLB resources are supported. OBJ MTL texture options need conversion to GLB or simpler references.

```sh
python -m explainer register-model explainer/projects/my_subject housing /path/to/model.glb \
  --rights /path/to/rights.json --evidence /path/to/source-license.txt \
  --meters-per-unit 1 --units-notes 'glTF 2.0 units are meters'
```

Registration leaves `assets.housing.review` as `pending`. Codex must inspect the actual asset before changing it to `approved`. Rights review and visual/accuracy review are separate. Nothing grants storyboard or preview approval.

An assembly component can reference it with:

```json
{"id":"housing_instance","shape":"model","asset_id":"housing","role":"structure",
 "position":[0,0,0],"scale":1,"rotation":[0,0,0],"move_to":[1,0,0]}
```

Also list `"housing"` in that shot's `asset_ids`. Imported geometry keeps its relative dimensions and materials; `scale` is uniform and unit conversion is explicit. Do not use a primitive `size` vector to distort an imported model. The assembly is centered at the component origin, so leaders track its center. Source cameras/lights and source animation are removed; static geometry/material import and whole-instance motion are supported. Individual source-part controls, animation retargeting and general imported-model sections are future adapters. `.blend`, scripts and native CAD formats are not accepted.

All referenced buffers, MTLs, textures and license evidence join the approval fingerprint. A texture-only change invalidates earlier approvals. Imported textures are packed into the saved Blender scene.

```sh
python -m explainer credits explainer/projects/my_subject
```

Final production also writes `CREDITS.md`. Include applicable credits/changes in the published video description; the engine does not publish or certify legal ownership. License declarations must reflect Codex's actual source review.

Optional actual Blender test: download the pinned CC0 specimen using the `download_url` and verify `download_sha256` in `examples/licenses/avocado-rights.json`; place it at `explainer/build/import-source/Avocado.glb`, then run `python -m explainer.tests.import_smoke`. It renders the real CC0 GLB and self-authored textured glTF/OBJ/STL fixtures. All registrations remain pending; diagnostic copies simulate asset review exclusively for isolated tests. No user approvals or full episode are created.

## Slider-crank visual pilot

`slider_crank.py` provides checked ideal crank-pin and slider positions for arbitrary valid radius/rod-length ratios. The six-second procedural cutaway pilot uses those positions to keep the rod at a constant length and the piston on its axis. It illustrates rotation converted to reciprocating motion; it does not simulate combustion, valves, lubrication or forces. The authored geometry uses no downloaded model assets. The detailed pilot render script currently lives in the ignored `build/piston-test/` experiment directory; it has not been added as a general declarative production adapter.

## Review and work pool

The Tesla first-chapter preview is reviewed before the full film. `review_queue.prepare_packet` requires passing media and actual visual review, and records **send to work pool / reject** as pending choices. After an actual user reply, `review_queue.decide` either preserves rejection notes or creates a source-snapshotted explainer project item in `explainer/work_pool/`. No task queues automatically. These items are deliberately distinct from Grandpa's render-ready scene queue: remaining chapters, assets and production preflight must still be completed.

"""Resumable complete-film production; final inspection is distinct from automated QA."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse, hashlib, math, shutil, subprocess, sys
from explainer.core import read, write
from explainer.media import voice, check_video, assemble, mix_mechanical

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT=ROOT/'build/full-v1'
FPS=30
AUTH="User: go ahead and send to pool and run the entire process, look is ok dress it up more on blank canvas going forward"
TITLES=['Opening','What Tesla disclosed','Why decision time matters','How search grows','Start with a goal','Layers of interaction','Relevant agents remain visible','Compare coherent choices','What scores can consider','Prune poor branches','Efficiency and hardware limits','Application versus deployment','Selective effort']
MODES=['opening','graph','latency','growth','traffic','layers','attention','traffic','scores','pruning','compute','evidence','graph']

def sha(p):return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
def run(args):subprocess.run([str(x) for x in args],check=True)

def prepare():
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    plan=read(ROOT/'plan.json');shots=[]
    opening=read(ROOT/'build/opening-v2/qa.json')
    decision=read(ROOT/'review/decision.json')
    assert decision['status']=='sent_to_work_pool'
    authorization=read(ROOT/'production-state.json')
    assert authorization.get('full_process_authorized') and authorization.get('user_authorization')==AUTH,'Full production needs actual recorded user authorization'
    for i,source in enumerate(plan['shots']):
        shot={key:source[key] for key in ['id','narration','claim_ids','teaches','simplifications']}
        shot.update(index=i,title=TITLES[i],mode=MODES[i],implementation='render_film_chapter.py')
        folder=OUT/shot['id'];folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        if i==0:
            shot.update(narration=opening['script'],seconds=opening['seconds'],frames=round(opening['seconds']*FPS),voice=opening['voice'],voice_sha256=opening['voice_sha256'])
        else:
            # Original dramatic plan used a truck; the verified teaching mechanism does
            # not require that class. Keep wording aligned with the actual vehicle prop.
            shot['narration']=shot['narration'].replace('truck','vehicle')
            meta=folder/'voice.json'
            if not meta.exists():voice(shot,folder)
            a=read(meta)
            assert a['text']==shot['narration'] and a['sha256']==sha(folder/'voice.wav')
            seconds=math.ceil((a['seconds']+.55)*FPS)/FPS
            shot.update(seconds=seconds,frames=round(seconds*FPS),voice=a['profile'],voice_sha256=a['sha256'])
        shot['duration']=shot['seconds']
        shot['visual_revision']='original-completed' if i<=2 else 'varied-camera-environments-v2'
        shots.append(shot)
    manifest={'title':plan['title'],'authorization':AUTH,'preview_decision':decision['id'],
              'fps':FPS,'width':960,'height':540,'render_samples':8,'shots':shots,
              'seconds':sum(s['seconds'] for s in shots),'music':False,'captions':False,
              'sources':plan['sources'],'accuracy':'All graphics are original schematic explanations; no proprietary Tesla software, measured score or deployment reconstruction.'}
    write(OUT/'manifest.json',manifest)
    md=['# Full-film production storyboard','',AUTH,'',f"Measured runtime: {manifest['seconds']:.1f} seconds. The approved opening is reused byte-for-byte.",'']
    for shot in shots:md.extend([f"## {shot['index']+1}. {shot['title']}",'',shot['narration'],'',f"Moving 3D scene: {shot['mode']}. Duration: {shot['seconds']:.2f}s.",''])
    (ROOT/'full-production-storyboard.md').write_text('\n'.join(md))
    (OUT/'CREDITS.md').write_text('# Sources and credits\n\nAll vehicle, road, environment, compute and graph geometry: original procedural project models. No downloaded models. Generic vehicles are not Tesla CAD.\n\nNarration: Kokoro am_fenrir. Graphics fonts: DejaVu Sans. No music.\n\nTechnical source: US20260105614A1, published April 16, 2026, https://patents.google.com/patent/US20260105614A1/en\n\nProduct limitations: https://www.tesla.com/support/fsd\n\nApplication disclosure is not evidence of deployment, hardware parity or measured performance.\n')
    return manifest

def encode(shot):
    folder=OUT/shot['id'];video=folder/'chapter.mp4'
    encode_sources={p.name:sha(p) for p in [Path(__file__),ROOT/'film_labels.py']}
    if video.exists() and (folder/'qa.json').exists():
        prior=read(folder/'qa.json')
        if prior['passed'] and prior.get('encode_source_hashes')==encode_sources:return video
    from PIL import Image
    from importlib import import_module
    decorate=import_module('explainer.projects.tesla-hw3.film_labels').decorate
    frames=folder/'frames';frames.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    expected={f'{i:06d}.png' for i in range(shot['frames'])}
    assert {p.name for p in (folder/'raw').glob('*.png')}==expected,'Incomplete chapter'
    filtered=folder/'filtered';filtered.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    run(['ffmpeg','-v','error','-y','-threads','2','-filter_threads','2','-framerate',FPS,'-i',folder/'raw/%06d.png','-vf','nlmeans=s=4:p=7:r=9','-start_number',0,filtered/'%06d.png'])
    poses=read(folder/'poses.json')
    for f in range(shot['frames']):
        with Image.open(filtered/f'{f:06d}.png') as src:im=src.convert('RGB')
        im=decorate(im,poses[str(f)])
        im.save(frames/f'{f:06d}.png')
    cues=[]
    if shot['mode'] in ['traffic','attention','latency']:
        start=0 if shot['mode']=='latency' else 6.7
        cues=[{'kind':'motor','at':start,'duration':shot['seconds']-start-.2,'purpose':'Quiet synthetic movement cue; not an authentic vehicle recording.'}]
    audio=mix_mechanical({'id':shot['id'],'sfx':cues},folder/'voice.wav',folder/'mix.wav',shot['seconds'])
    gain=0
    for _ in range(4):
        run(['ffmpeg','-v','error','-y','-framerate',FPS,'-i',frames/'%06d.png','-i',audio,'-af',f'volume={gain:.3f}dB,alimiter=limit=0.65:level=false:latency=1,apad','-t',shot['seconds'],'-c:v','libx264','-threads',2,'-crf',18,'-pix_fmt','yuv420p','-c:a','aac','-ar',48000,'-movflags','+faststart',video])
        qa=check_video(video,shot['seconds'],960,540)
        if qa['passed']:break
        gain+=-14-qa['lufs']
    assert qa['passed'],qa
    qa.update(review='pending_final_sequence_inspection',voice_sha256=shot['voice_sha256'],scene_checks=read(folder/'scene-qa.json'),encode_source_hashes=encode_sources)
    write(folder/'qa.json',qa)
    # Retain native frames and media; disposable denoise/compositing copies are reproducible.
    shutil.rmtree(filtered);shutil.rmtree(frames)
    return video

def main():
    a=argparse.ArgumentParser();a.add_argument('--prepare',action='store_true');a.add_argument('--preflight',action='store_true');a.add_argument('--render',action='store_true');args=a.parse_args()
    m=prepare()
    if args.prepare:return
    renderer='explainer.projects.tesla-hw3.render_film_chapter'
    if args.preflight:
        for shot in m['shots'][3:]:run([sys.executable,'-m',renderer,'--index',shot['index'],'--stills'])
        write(OUT/'pipeline-state.json',{'stage':'preflight_images_ready','full_render_started':False,'seconds':m['seconds']})
        return
    if not args.render:return
    review=read(OUT/'preflight-review.json')
    assert review['passed'],'Actual preflight images must be inspected first'
    for path,expected in review['source_hashes'].items():
        assert sha(path)==expected,('Preflight review is stale',path)
    assert review['manifest_sha256']==sha(OUT/'manifest.json'),'Measured production manifest changed after review'
    videos=[ROOT/'build/opening-v2/tesla-opening-v2.mp4']
    for shot in m['shots'][1:]:
        if shot['index']<=2:
            folder=OUT/shot['id'];video=folder/'chapter.mp4'
            completed=read(folder/'qa.json')
            assert video.exists() and completed['passed'],'Previously completed chapter is missing'
            assert completed['voice_sha256']==shot['voice_sha256'],'Completed narration no longer matches the film'
            videos.append(video)
            continue
        write(OUT/'pipeline-state.json',{'stage':'rendering','chapter':shot['index']+1,'title':shot['title'],'total_chapters':len(m['shots']),'full_render_started':True})
        run([sys.executable,'-m',renderer,'--index',shot['index']])
        videos.append(encode(shot))
    output=OUT/'tesla-planning-complete.mp4'
    assemble(videos,[s['seconds'] for s in m['shots']],output)
    qa=check_video(output,m['seconds'],960,540);assert qa['passed'],qa
    qa.update(review='pending_actual_final_video_inspection',scope='Complete film',chapters=len(videos))
    write(OUT/'final-qa.json',qa)
    write(OUT/'pipeline-state.json',{'stage':'complete_media_pending_final_inspection','full_render_started':True,'video':str(output),'seconds':m['seconds'],'automatic_publication':False})
    print('FULL FILM ENCODED; FINAL INSPECTION REQUIRED',output,flush=True)

if __name__=='__main__':
    try:main()
    except Exception as error:
        OUT.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        write(OUT/'pipeline-error.json',{'stage':'stopped_on_error','error':str(error),'automatic_publication':False})
        raise

"""Moving 3D search-tree opening. Miniature worlds are illustrative candidate states."""

from explainer.blender_backend import aim

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
TEXT = ("How does a car's computer choose its next move without wasting effort on poor choices? "
        "A Tesla patent application describes one approach: score the choices, cut poor branches early, "
        "and develop more promising ones. Here's how that search works—and what it actually proves.")
if not (OUT / 'voice.json').exists():
    voice({'narration': TEXT}, OUT)
audio = read(OUT / 'voice.json')

FPS = 30
DURATION = math.ceil((audio['seconds'] + .55) * FPS) / FPS
NF = round(DURATION * FPS)
W, H = 640, 360
write(OUT / 'timing.json', {'seconds': DURATION, 'frames': NF, 'script': TEXT,
      'voice': audio['profile'], 'speech_wpm': audio['measured_words_per_minute'],
      'position_in_film': 'opening, from 00:00', 'width': W, 'height': H})

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
s = bpy.context.scene
s.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
s.cycles.samples = 12
s.cycles.use_denoising = False
s.cycles.max_bounces = 3
s.cycles.diffuse_bounces = 1
s.cycles.glossy_bounces = 2
s.render.threads_mode = 'FIXED'
s.render.threads = 4
s.render.resolution_x, s.render.resolution_y = W, H
s.render.resolution_percentage = 100
s.render.fps = FPS
s.frame_start, s.frame_end = 0, NF-1
s.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('Soft studio')
s.world.use_nodes = True
s.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[0].default_value = (.24, .32, .43, 1)
s.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[1].default_value = .7

def matte(name, color):
    m = material(name, color)
    sh = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
    sh.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = 0
    sh.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = .78
    return m

floor = matte('Studio backdrop', (.025, .045, .07, 1))
asphalt = matte('Road', (.055, .07, .09, 1))
platform = matte('Sectioned world', (.19, .25, .30, 1))
white = matte('Lane paint', (.76, .83, .86, 1))
cyan = material('Develop promising choice', (.025, .68, .88, 1), True)
gray = material('Candidate link', (.26, .36, .43, 1), True)
red = material('Low scoring branch', (.92, .14, .07, 1), True)
orange = matte('Pedestrian coat', (.8, .34, .035, 1))
dark = matte('Pedestrian trousers', (.04, .055, .075, 1))
skin = matte('Pedestrian head', (.55, .32, .18, 1))
cube('Studio floor', (0, 5, -.7), (250, 250, .6), floor, bevel=0)

def clone_tree(source, name, parent):
    copies = {}
    def visit(obj, par):
        cp = obj.copy()
        cp.name = name + ' ' + obj.name
        s.collection.objects.link(cp)
        cp.parent = par
        copies[obj] = cp
        for child in obj.children:
            visit(child, cp)
        return cp
    root = visit(source, parent)
    root.location = (0, 0, 0)
    return root

blue_template = build_vehicle('Blue EV')
red_template = build_vehicle('Oncoming EV', (.48, .065, .035, 1))
worlds = []

def world(name, location, kind):
    root = bpy.data.objects.new(name, None)
    s.collection.objects.link(root)
    root.location = location
    slab = cube(name + ' base', (0, 0, -.18), (15, 22, .36), platform, root, .25)
    cube(name + ' vertical road', (0, 0, .015), (7.3, 22, .06), asphalt, root, .015)
    cube(name + ' crossing road', (0, 0, .02), (15, 7.3, .06), asphalt, root, .015)
    for sign in [-1, 1]:
        for x in [-2.9, -1.8, -.7, .4, 1.5, 2.6]:
            cube(name + ' crossing', (x, sign*4.6, .065), (.55, 1.1, .016), white, root, 0)
        cube(name + ' lane', (0, sign*6.5, .06), (.10, 1.7, .018), white, root, 0)
        cube(name + ' exit lane', (sign*6.4, 0, .06), (1.7, .10, .018), white, root, 0)
    car = clone_tree(blue_template, name, root)
    other = clone_tree(red_template, name, root)
    other.rotation_euler.z = math.pi
    cube(name + ' stop line', (1.8, -5.45, .07), (3.3, .12, .02), white, root, 0)
    pedestrian = None
    legs = []
    if kind in ('present', 'creep', 'wait'):
        pedestrian = bpy.data.objects.new(name + ' pedestrian', None)
        s.collection.objects.link(pedestrian)
        pedestrian.parent = root
        cube(name + ' coat', (0, 0, 1.18), (.43, .27, .59), orange, pedestrian, .08)
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=16, ring_count=8, radius=.16, location=(0, 0, 1.64))
        head = bpy.context.object
        head.parent = pedestrian
        head.data.materials.append(skin)
        for sign in [-1, 1]:
            leg = cube(name + ' leg', (sign*.12, 0, .51), (.15, .19, .78), dark, pedestrian, .06)
            cube(name + ' shoe', (sign*.12, .035, .105), (.17, .30, .18), dark, pedestrian, .035)
            arm = cube(name + ' arm', (sign*.29, 0, 1.13), (.13, .16, .55), orange, pedestrian, .05)
            legs.append((sign, leg, arm))
    wheel_sets = [(vehicle, [o for o in vehicle.children if o.get('vehicle_part') == 'wheel'])
                  for vehicle in [car, other]]
    # A road-level target marker identifies the desired left-turn exit.
    marker = line(name + ' goal', [(-5.7, 1.8, .10), (-6.4, 1.8, .10), (-6.0, 2.15, .10)], .07, cyan)
    marker.parent = root
    item = {'root': root, 'base': slab, 'car': car, 'other': other, 'kind': kind,
            'wheels': wheel_sets, 'location': Vector(location), 'pedestrian': pedestrian, 'limbs': legs}
    worlds.append(item)
    return item

base = world('Present', (0, -20, 0), 'present')
choices = [world('Turn now', (-22, 6, .2), 'early'),
           world('Creep forward', (0, 6, .2), 'creep'),
           world('Wait', (22, 6, .2), 'wait')]
future = [world('Next turn', (13, 32, .4), 'turn'),
          world('Next wait', (31, 32, .4), 'later_wait')]
# Source templates are removed; linked copies retain their mesh datablocks.
for template in [blue_template, red_template]:
    for obj in [*template.children_recursive, template]:
        bpy.data.objects.remove(obj, do_unlink=True)

def edge(name, a, b):
    return line(name, [(a[0], a[1]+11.0, .2), ((a[0]+b[0])/2, (a[1]+b[1])/2, .7),
                       (b[0], b[1]-11.0, b[2]+.2)], .10, gray)
links = [edge('Candidate ' + str(i), base['location'], w['location']) for i, w in enumerate(choices)]
next_links = [edge('Further search ' + str(i), choices[2]['location'], w['location']) for i, w in enumerate(future)]

for name, pos, power, size in [('Key', (-18, -20, 45), 42000, 32),
                              ('Fill', (35, 10, 38), 31000, 26)]:
    data = bpy.data.lights.new(name, 'AREA')
    data.energy, data.size = power, size
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, data)
    s.collection.objects.link(obj)
    obj.location = pos
    aim(obj, (6, 0, 0))

cam = bpy.context.object
s.camera = cam
cam.data.dof.use_dof = False
cam.data.clip_end = 400

def ease(v):
    v = min(1, max(0, v))
    return v*v*(3-2*v)

def set_cars(w, u):
    """Each tile is an alternative schematic state, not simultaneous physical traffic."""
    k = w['kind']
    car, other = w['car'], w['other']
    car.rotation_euler.z = 0
    x, y, yaw, distance = 1.8, -7.6, 0, 0
    if k == 'present':
        distance = 1.0*ease(u/.24)
        y = -8.6+distance
    elif k == 'early':
        # A speculative early turn approaches the oncoming path; it stops before contact.
        q = ease((u-.27)/.28)
        theta = q*.58
        x, y, yaw = -2.5+4.3*math.cos(theta), -2.5+4.3*math.sin(theta), theta
        distance = 3.8+theta*4.3
    elif k == 'creep':
        distance = 2.1*ease((u-.28)/.28)
        y += distance
    elif k == 'turn':
        q = ease((u-.72)/.28)
        theta = q*math.pi/2
        x, y, yaw = -2.5+4.3*math.cos(theta), -2.5+4.3*math.sin(theta), theta
        distance = 3.8+theta*4.3
    car.location, car.rotation_euler.z = (x, y, .08), yaw
    if k == 'early':
        other.location = (-1.8, 6.5-1.5*ease((u-.27)/.28), .08)
    else:
        other.location = (-1.8, 6.5-12*ease((u-.16)/.70), .08)
    if w['pedestrian'] is not None:
        progress = ease((u-.25)/.25)
        w['pedestrian'].location = (4.8-1.5*progress, -4.6, .08)
        w['pedestrian'].rotation_euler.z = math.pi/2
        for sign, leg, arm in w['limbs']:
            angle = .3*math.sin(progress*math.tau*1.5+(0 if sign < 0 else math.pi))
            leg.rotation_euler.x = angle
            arm.rotation_euler.x = -angle
    for vehicle, wheels in w['wheels']:
        d = distance if vehicle == car else 6.5-other.location.y
        for wheel in wheels:
            wheel.rotation_euler.x = -d/.34
            wheel.rotation_euler.z = .35 if vehicle == car and yaw > .01 and wheel.location.y > 0 else 0
    assert not rectangles_overlap((x, y, yaw), (other.location.x, other.location.y, math.pi)), ('Vehicle overlap', k, u)

poses = {}
lenses = {'car_question': 50, 'possible_futures': 31,
          'evaluate_and_prune': 28, 'develop_next_choices': 29}
def apply(f):
    u = f / max(1, NF-1)
    for w in worlds:
        set_cars(w, u)
    for i, (w, link) in enumerate(zip(choices, links)):
        grow = ease((u-.24-i*.025)/.13)
        remove = ease((u-.60-i*.025)/.12) if i < 2 else 0
        scale = max(.0001, grow*(1-remove))
        w['root'].scale = (scale,)*3
        link.data.bevel_factor_end = grow*(1-remove)
        link.data.materials[0] = (red if i == 0 else gray) if u > .49 else gray
        if i == 2 and u > .49:
            link.data.materials[0] = cyan
    for i, (w, link) in enumerate(zip(future, next_links)):
        grow = ease((u-.71-i*.035)/.16)
        w['root'].scale = (max(.0001, grow),)*3
        link.data.bevel_factor_end = grow
        link.data.materials[0] = cyan
    if u < .24:
        q = u/.24
        cam.location = (9-2*q, -17-q, 4.5+.4*q)
        target = Vector((2, -27.3, .7))
        lens, shot, important = 48, 'car_question', [base['car']]
    elif u < .49:
        q = (u-.24)/.25
        cam.location = (37-7*q, -58+2*q, 55+4*q)
        target = Vector((0, -5, 0))
        lens, shot, important = 31, 'possible_futures', [base['base'], *[w['base'] for w in choices]]
    elif u < .69:
        q = (u-.49)/.20
        cam.location = (12-5*q, -35+q, 42)
        target = Vector((0, 6, 0))
        lens, shot, important = 28, 'evaluate_and_prune', [w['base'] for w in choices]
    else:
        q = (u-.69)/.31
        cam.location = (57-5*q, -34+6*q, 58)
        target = Vector((20, 17+3*q, .2))
        lens, shot, important = 25, 'develop_next_choices', [choices[2]['base'], *[w['base'] for w in future]]
    cam.data.lens = lenses[shot]
    aim(cam, target)
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    # Widen framing once for the entire shot, rather than per-frame lens pumping.
    projected = {}
    for w in worlds:
        p = world_to_camera_view(s, cam, w['root'].matrix_world @ Vector((0, -11.6, .1)))
        projected[w['kind']] = [p.x, 1-p.y, w['root'].scale.x]
    bad = []
    focal_ratio = 1.0
    for obj in important:
        if obj.parent and obj.parent.scale.x < .03:
            continue
        meshes = [o for o in obj.children_recursive if o.type == 'MESH'] if obj.type == 'EMPTY' else [obj]
        for mesh in meshes:
            for corner in mesh.bound_box:
                p = world_to_camera_view(s, cam, mesh.matrix_world @ Vector(corner))
                if p.z <= 0:
                    raise ValueError(('Object behind camera', f, mesh.name))
                focal_ratio = min(focal_ratio, .475/max(abs(p.x-.5), 1e-9),
                                  .44/max(abs(p.y-.5), 1e-9))
                if p.z <= 0 or not (.025 < p.x < .975 and .055 < p.y < .96):
                    bad.append(mesh.name)
                    break
    poses[f] = {'shot': shot, 'labels': projected, 'bad_bounds': sorted(set(bad)),
                'visible_candidates': sum(w['root'].scale.x > .03 for w in choices),
                'next_choices': sum(w['root'].scale.x > .03 for w in future),
                'focal_ratio': focal_ratio,
                'car_positions': {w['kind']: list(w['car'].location) for w in worlds}}
    return bad

for attempt in range(3):
    for f in range(NF):
        apply(f)
    bad = {f: p['bad_bounds'] for f, p in poses.items() if p['bad_bounds']}
    if not bad:
        break
    for shot in lenses:
        ratio = min(p['focal_ratio'] for p in poses.values() if p['shot'] == shot)
        if ratio < 1:
            lenses[shot] *= ratio*.97
    print('Constant-per-shot camera repair', attempt+1, lenses, flush=True)
assert not bad, f'Camera bounds need repair: {dict(list(bad.items())[:3])}'
assert poses[round(NF*.47)]['visible_candidates'] == 3
assert poses[round(NF*.92)]['visible_candidates'] == 1
assert poses[round(NF*.98)]['next_choices'] == 2
write(OUT / 'poses.json', poses)
write(OUT / 'scene-qa.json', {'frames': NF, 'all_frame_bounds_passed': True,
      'choices_before_pruning': 3, 'choices_after_pruning': 1, 'expanded_choices': 2,
      'camera_shots': sorted(set(p['shot'] for p in poses.values())),

                engine/'visual_tools.py', engine/'blender_backend.py', engine/'turn_motion.py', OUT/'voice.wav']

"""Finish the continuous-3D search opening; freeze narration and leave review pending.

Run only after opening_search.py has completed every native 30-fps frame.
Spatial denoising avoids temporal trails on moving geometry; no frame interpolation,
held images, narration captions, music or recorded-speech time stretching.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import subprocess
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
from explainer.core import read, write
from explainer.media import check_video

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / 'build/opening-v2'
W, H, FPS = 960, 540, 30
FONT_DIR = Path('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu')


def font(size, bold=False):
    return ImageFont.truetype(str(FONT_DIR / ('DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf' if bold else 'DejaVuSans.ttf')), size)


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def overlay(im, pose, u):
    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (W, H))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
    boxes = []
    shot = pose['shot']
    if shot != 'car_question':
        for key, title in [('early', 'TURN NOW'), ('creep', 'CREEP'), ('wait', 'WAIT'),
                           ('turn', 'NEXT CHOICES'), ('later_wait', 'NEXT CHOICES')]:
            x, y, scale = pose['labels'][key]
            threshold = .90 if key in ('turn', 'later_wait') else .85
            if scale <= threshold or not (.025 < x < .975 and .025 < y < .91):
                continue
            descriptor = ''
            color = '#d4e1e8'
            if shot == 'evaluate_and_prune' and u > .49 and key in ('early', 'creep', 'wait'):
                descriptor = {'early': 'CONFLICT AHEAD', 'creep': 'BLOCKS CROSSWALK', 'wait': 'EXPAND'}[key]
                color = '#5edbed' if key == 'wait' else '#f0b58d'
            elif key in ('turn', 'later_wait'):
                color = '#5edbed'
            f = font(18, True)
            sub = font(12, True)
            width = max(d.textlength(title, font=f), d.textlength(descriptor, font=sub)) + 20
            height = 46 if descriptor else 30
            cx, top = x*W, y*H+3
            box = (round(cx-width/2), round(top), round(cx+width/2), round(top+height))
            # Do not slide detached labels into the frame or let neighboring badges overlap.
            if box[0] < 14 or box[2] > W-14 or box[1] < 10 or box[3] > H-32:
                continue
            if any(box[0] < b[2]+5 and box[2] > b[0]-5 and box[1] < b[3]+3 and box[3] > b[1]-3 for b in boxes):
                continue
            alpha = round(235*min(1, max(0, (scale-threshold)/(1-threshold))))
            d.rounded_rectangle(box, radius=5, fill=(8, 23, 34, alpha), outline=(68, 100, 117, alpha), width=1)
            d.text((cx, top+5), title, font=f, fill=color, anchor='mt')
            if descriptor:
                d.text((cx, top+29), descriptor, font=sub, fill=color, anchor='mt')
            boxes.append(box)
    footer = 'Illustrative search · not Tesla software or measured performance'
    d.text((16, H-18), footer, font=font(11), fill='#d1dce5', stroke_width=2, stroke_fill=(8, 18, 27, 190))
    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'), layer).convert('RGB'), boxes


def main():
    timing = read(OUT / 'timing.json')
    poses = read(OUT / 'poses.json')
    nf, seconds = timing['frames'], timing['seconds']
    if nf != 453 or abs(seconds*FPS-nf) > .001:
        raise ValueError(f'Unexpected opening version/timing: {nf} frames, {seconds} seconds')
    expected = {f'{i:06d}.png' for i in range(nf)}
    actual = {p.name for p in (OUT / 'raw').glob('*.png')}
    if actual != expected:
        raise ValueError(f'Incomplete render: {len(actual)}/{nf}; missing {sorted(expected-actual)[:5]}, extras {sorted(actual-expected)[:5]}')
    if set(poses) != {str(i) for i in range(nf)}:
        raise ValueError('Incomplete motion/label poses')
    audio = OUT / 'voice.wav'
    voice_hash = sha(audio)
    if voice_hash != read(OUT / 'voice.json')['sha256']:
        raise ValueError('Frozen voice bytes changed')
    filtered, frames = OUT / 'filtered', OUT / 'frames'
    filtered.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    frames.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-v', 'error', '-y', '-threads', '2', '-filter_threads', '2',
        '-framerate', str(FPS), '-start_number', '0', '-i', str(OUT / 'raw/%06d.png'),
        '-vf', 'nlmeans=s=5:p=7:r=9,scale=960:540:flags=lanczos', '-frames:v', str(nf),
        '-start_number', '0', str(filtered / '%06d.png')], check=True)
    label_boxes = {}
    selected = [0, round(nf*.20), round(nf*.37), round(nf*.51), round(nf*.58), round(nf*.68), round(nf*.86), nf-1]
    for i in range(nf):
        with Image.open(filtered / f'{i:06d}.png') as raw:
